correctness.rationale: For real BV the positive and negative parts of Df have mass V(f)/2. Their product coupling writes the residual as V(f)/2 times the mean of the residuals of oriented arcs. In an equality case the arc residuals all have maximal norm and zero Hilbert-space variance, so they agree almost surely. Injectivity modulo constants gives the same ordered pair of derivative atoms. Parseval, the two frequencies ±n and V(1_arc)=2 give the stated 1/(2π²) coefficient, and continuity on [0,1/2] gives attainment. On the line the step residual is (sgn x)/2 times erfc(|x|/(2√t)); the inner product between two translates has absolute bound √(2πt) exp(−separation²/(8t))/4. Summing shifts at distances at least |k|−1/2 proves the exponentially small, uniform error needed for varying maximizing lengths. The line rescaling v=2π√t|ξ| gives √t F(d/(2√t)). Splitting the unregularized Dirichlet term from the Gaussian terms gives F′=erfc(z)−erfc(z/√2)/2. The increasing Gaussian hazard makes the tail ratio strictly increasing from 1 to infinity. The unique maximum lies strictly above the limit at infinity, so every maximizing rescaled length converges. Independent bisection on [0,2] with erfc rechecked the stated constants; higher-precision bisection using the alternating erf series on [0.9,1.1] gave z*=0.992269655382049579 and F(z*)=0.198313496197009020. The prefactor rounds to 0.445324035054261 at 15 decimal places (one final digit different from the frozen decimal); the exact formula is unaffected.
